title: Kinematic Constraints of Pure Rolling and the Instantaneous Center of Rotation
learning_objective: Formulate the no-slip contact constraint for rolling bodies and determine instantaneous velocities of all body points using the Instantaneous Center of Rotation.
explanation: Pure rolling without slipping is a combined translational-rotational motion characterized by the kinematic constraint that the relative velocity between the contact point $P$ of the rolling body and the supporting surface is identically zero at every instant: $$\vec{v}_P = \vec{v}_{\text{cm}} + \vec{\omega} \times \vec{r}_{P/\text{cm}} = \vec{0}$$ For a wheel of radius $R$ rolling on a stationary planar surface, this constraint yields the fundamental relations: $$v_{\text{cm}} = R \omega, \quad a_{\text{cm}} = R \alpha$$ At any given instant, the contact point $P$ is momentarily at rest in the ground frame and serves as the Instantaneous Center of Rotation (ICR). The entire velocity field of the rigid body corresponds to pure rotation about $P$ with angular speed $\omega$. Consequently, the top rim point $T$ has velocity $v_T = 2 v_{\text{cm}} = 2 R \omega$, and any point at distance $r$ from $P$ has instantaneous speed $v = r \omega$. Although $P$ has zero instantaneous velocity, its acceleration is non-zero: $\vec{a}_P = \omega^2 R \hat{j}$, pointing vertically upward toward the center.
intuition: When a wheel rolls without slipping, each point on the rim touches the ground for a single instant before peeling off along a cycloid. At that precise instant of contact, it is not sliding across the ground at all—it is momentarily stationary, like the foot of a walking person planted on the pavement.
formal_definition: The kinematic condition of zero relative tangential velocity between two contacting rigid surfaces at their point of contact: $$\vec{v}_{\text{contact, rel}} = \vec{v}_{\text{body}}(P) - \vec{v}_{\text{surface}}(P) = \vec{0}$$
assumptions: Rigid circular cross-section (cylinder, sphere, wheel) of radius R
Zero microscopic sliding or slipping at the contact interface
boundary_conditions: Valid provided static friction is sufficient to enforce zero relative velocity
Fails during skidding, locking, or spinning where v_cm != R omega
source_references: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Chapter 11, Section 11.1 (Rolling as Pure Rotation)
University Physics, Chapter 10, Section 10.3 (Combined Translation and Rotation)
